newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Oct fishmeal output down 70 pct vs yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Oct fishmeal output down 70 pct vs yr ago.

text.p: Peru produced 37,300 tonnes of fishmeal in October, down 70 percent from the same month last year, the government said Thursday.
A Fisheries' Ministry report added that fishmeal production in the first ten months of the year was 1.261 million tonnes, down 13.5 percent compared with the same period last year.
Exports of fishmeal for October, however, rose 38.6 percent to 78,900 tonnes, compared with the same month last year.

Exports for the first ten months were down 16.5 percent to 1.278 million tonnes, compared with the same period the year before. The value of these exports between January and October rose, however, by 14.8 percent to $670.51 million.
Officials have said the country's fishmeal production has fallen due to seasonal fishing bans and climatic factors while higher world prices have brought the overall hike in the value of exports.

Fishmeal, Peru's most important fishing product, accounted for 65.5 percent of Peru's total processing of 56,900 tonnes of fish and other sea products in October, and 73.9 percent of the ten-month total of 1.707 million tonnes.

Production of Peru's second most important fish product, raw fish oil, was 2,500 tonnes in October, down from 22,100 in the same month last year. Output of raw fish oil in the first ten months was 287.6 million tonnes, 10.1 percent lower than in the same period last year.

In October, the total catch of Peruvian fish and sea species was down to 210,500 tonnes from 667,200 in the same month last year. The total catch for the first ten months fell 11.9 percent to 6.48 million tonnes.

Peru produced 1.77 million tonnes of fishmeal in 1995, down 24.1 percent from the 2.34 million tonnes processed the previous year. However, the value of fishmeal exports last year rose 4.1 percent to $766.54 million despite an 18.2 percent drop in the volume sold abroad to 1.86 million tonnes.

According to the government's National Institute of Statistics and Information (INEI), the fishing sector's year- on-year output contracted 52.3 percent in October and 7.9 percent in the first ten months of the year.
Economy Minister Jorge Camet told Congress in September he expects the fishing industry to recover next year and grow by five percent.
